packages.title: Agriculture around 13 percent UK GHG QA
facts: Defra states agriculture accounts for around 13% of UK greenhouse gases.
The statement refers to a national sector share.
Agricultural GHGs include nitrous oxide, methane and carbon dioxide.
Ammonia is also reported but is an air pollutant rather than a greenhouse-gas total.
The national sector share is not a farm-parcel measurement.

packages.title: Agriculture 59 percent of UK nitrous oxide QA
facts: Agriculture accounted for 59% of UK nitrous oxide emissions in 2024.
The figure is a share of national nitrous oxide emissions.
Nitrous oxide is one greenhouse gas in the agricultural inventory.
Inventory data are revised as methodologies improve.
The share is not an individual field measurement.

packages.title: Agriculture 49 percent of UK methane QA
facts: Agriculture accounted for 49% of UK methane emissions in 2024.
The figure is a national methane share.
Agricultural methane is dominated by livestock-related sources.
The inventory estimate is subject to methodological revision.
No livestock holding or parcel value is inferred from the national share.

packages.title: Agriculture 2.5 percent of UK carbon dioxide QA
facts: Agriculture accounted for 2.5% of UK carbon-dioxide emissions in 2024.
This share concerns CO2 specifically rather than total greenhouse gases.
It is much smaller than agriculture's shares of methane and nitrous oxide.
Gas-specific shares must not be merged without CO2e-compatible accounting.
The national share is not a parcel emission value.

packages.title: Agriculture 89 percent ammonia non-GHG guard QA
facts: Agriculture accounted for 89% of UK ammonia emissions in 2024.
Ammonia affects air quality but is not part of the greenhouse-gas total reported in CO2e.
Air-pollutant and greenhouse-gas metrics must remain separate.
The statistic is national in scope.
No parcel GHG value is derived from ammonia share.

packages.title: Agricultural nitrous oxide 12 MtCO2e 2024 QA
facts: Agricultural nitrous oxide emissions were about 12 MtCO2e in 2024 in Defra's table.
The corresponding 1990 value was about 16 MtCO2e.
The values are inventory estimates expressed as CO2e.
They concern the agriculture sector nationally.
They do not directly measure emissions from a selected parcel.

packages.title: Agricultural nitrous oxide decline since 1990 QA
facts: Agricultural nitrous oxide emissions were estimated to have fallen about 26% between 1990 and 2024.
Defra links the trend with fertiliser-use trends.
Methodological revisions can alter historical inventory values.
The trend concerns sector-level inventory emissions.
A national long-term trend is not applied to individual fields.

packages.title: Agricultural methane 27 MtCO2e 2024 QA
facts: Agricultural methane emissions were about 27 MtCO2e in 2024 in Defra's table.
The corresponding 1990 value was about 33 MtCO2e.
Methane values are expressed on a CO2e basis in the comparison.
The estimate concerns UK agriculture as a sector.
No parcel or herd measurement is inferred.

packages.title: Agricultural methane decline since 1990 QA
facts: Agricultural methane emissions were estimated to have fallen 18% between 1990 and 2024.
Defra attributes much of the reduction to decreasing livestock numbers.
The trend is an inventory estimate.
Livestock activity data and methane emissions are related but distinct measures.
The sector trend is not a parcel-specific change.

packages.title: Agricultural nitrous-oxide soil-source QA
facts: Defra identifies agricultural soils as the main source of agricultural nitrous oxide.
Nitrogen fertiliser application contributes to the source.
Applied and pasture-excreted manure also contribute.
Leaching and run-off are included among contributing processes.
Source categories do not provide a measured value for an individual parcel.

packages.title: Agricultural methane enteric-fermentation QA
facts: Defra identifies enteric fermentation in ruminating animals as the majority source of agricultural methane.
Manure management accounts for the remainder described in the publication.
Enteric fermentation is an emissions source category.
Livestock counts alone are not equivalent to measured methane emissions.
No farm-specific methane value is created without compatible activity and methodology evidence.

packages.title: Agriculture emissions long-term reduction summary QA
facts: Defra's 2025 agriculture publication states estimated greenhouse-gas and air-pollution emissions from agriculture fell 15% between 1990 and 2024.
The summary spans greenhouse-gas and air-pollution context.
It must not be re-labelled as a single gas-specific rate.
Underlying emissions series are revised as methods improve.
The summary trend is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey GHG decision importance QA
facts: In the 2026 Farm Practices Survey, 54% of farms considered GHGs fairly or very important in decisions about land, crops and livestock.
The figure is a survey proportion of holdings.
It measures reported decision importance rather than emissions.
Survey responses are not direct GHG measurements.
The percentage is not assigned to an individual parcel.

packages.title: Farm GHG-action recycling response QA
facts: Among farms taking action to reduce GHG emissions, 75% reported recycling farm waste materials in 2026.
The figure is a reported action proportion.
An action count does not quantify avoided GHG emissions.
The statistic comes from the Farm Practices Survey.
No parcel emissions reduction is inferred.

packages.title: Farm GHG-action energy-efficiency response QA
facts: Among farms taking GHG-reduction action, 69% reported improving energy efficiency in 2026.
The statistic is a proportion of holdings reporting an action.
Energy-efficiency activity does not itself provide measured CO2e savings.
Actual impacts depend on farm-specific activity and energy data.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Farm reduced-tillage action QA
facts: Among farms taking GHG-reduction action, 68% reported reducing tillage or using no tillage in 2026.
The percentage describes reported practice adoption.
Practice adoption is not a measured greenhouse-gas flux.
Soil-carbon or fuel effects require separate measurement or modelling.
No parcel reduction value is fabricated.

packages.title: Farm nitrogen-application accuracy action QA
facts: Among farms taking GHG-reduction action, 59% reported improving nitrogen fertiliser application accuracy in 2026.
The statistic is survey-reported practice adoption.
Nitrogen-management activity is not itself an N2O emissions measurement.
Emission effects depend on application, soil and inventory methodology.
No field-level N2O amount is inferred.

packages.title: Farm manure and slurry efficiency action QA
facts: In 2026, 45% of farms taking GHG-reduction action reported improved manure or slurry management and application efficiency.
The comparable reported share was 28% in 2013 when the question was first asked.
The series measures reported practice rather than verified emissions savings.
Manure management is relevant to methane and nitrous-oxide sources.
No farm-level emissions reduction is calculated from the survey percentage.

packages.title: Methane-suppressing feed adoption QA
facts: The 2026 Farm Practices Survey reports 2% of farms regularly fed methane-suppressing feed products to livestock.
The figure describes reported adoption.
It is not a measurement of methane reduction achieved.
Livestock and feed context would be required to estimate effects.
No parcel or herd emissions saving is inferred.

packages.title: Agricultural inventory annual revision guard QA
facts: Defra notes greenhouse-gas emissions data are revised each year for methodological improvements in the UK emissions inventory.
Historical values can therefore change between editions.
Publication vintage must be retained with each extracted value.
Revisions are not automatically errors.
Parcel values must not be back-calculated from revised national series.
